title: Proving Uniqueness of Real Roots via Rolle's Theorem
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Prove that the equation x^3 + 3x + 1 = 0 has exactly one real solution.
finalAnswer: \text{The equation has exactly one real root (at least one by IVT, at most one by Rolle's Theorem)}

steps.title: Prove Existence of at Least One Root (IVT)
steps.why: Guarantees at least one real root.

steps.title: Assume Two Roots and Apply Rolle's Theorem
steps.mathExpression: \text{Suppose } f(a) = f(b) = 0 \text{ with } a < b \implies \exists c \in (a, b) \text{ s.t. } f'(c) = 0
steps.explanation: If two roots existed, Rolle's Theorem would require f'(c) = 0.

steps.title: Demonstrate Contradiction with Derivative
steps.explanation: f'(x) is strictly positive everywhere; it can never equal 0.
steps.why: Contradiction implies f can have at most one real root.
